🎬 JUNIOR ANIMATOR GUIDE — V6
1. 🎯 OBJECTIVE
Produce short AI-generated videos (1–2 minutes), composed of multiple shots.
Each shot must communicate one clear idea, show one dominant visual element (anchor), and
include one micro-action.
Priority: Clarity > Consistency > Speed > Visual quality.
2. 🎯 FINAL EXPECTATION
A correct shot is instantly understandable (<1 second), focused on one visual element, simple
and mobile-readable, consistent with other shots, and slightly animated (micro-action only).
3. 🧠 CORE SYSTEM
Each shot follows: Line → Anchor → Shot.
Line = narration (voice + subtitles).
Anchor = key visual element.
Shot = how the anchor is shown with a micro-action.
This is non-negotiable.
4. 🔴 GOLDEN RULES
One idea per shot.
Anchor visible in <1 second, concrete, dominant.
One micro-action per shot.
No static images. No complex animation. Simplicity over beauty.
Frame composition includes foreground (anchor), background, and depth.
If not understood in <1 second → wrong.
5. 🔁 EXECUTION WORKFLOW
Pipeline: Storyboard → Pattern → Prompt → Generate → Animate → Voice → Subtitles →
Validate.
1. 	Read full episode (do not generate immediately).
2. 	Identify Line, Anchor, and type (Action / Reaction / Reveal / Tension / Transition).
3. 	Select pattern (see Section 6).
4. 	Build prompt (see Annex).
5. 	Generate image (anchor visible instantly, composition clear).
6. 	Add one micro-animation.
7. 	Add voice (match duration).
8. 	Add subtitles (match voice, readable).
9. 	Validate (one idea, clear anchor, readable, consistent).
10. Move to next shot.

-- 1 of 9 --

6. 🔧 PATTERN SELECTION (PRACTICAL)
Ask: “What is physically happening on screen?”
• 	Someone interacts → HAND / OBJECT
• 	Someone moves → FOOTSTEP / PATH
• 	Someone reacts → EYES / HEAD
• 	Something appears → REVEAL / SHADOW
• 	Nothing moves but tension → STILLNESS
Rule: if you hesitate, your pattern is too abstract → choose a more concrete one.
Example: “He is scared” → ❌ abstract → ✅ EYES — REACTION.
If multiple actions exist, choose the one the viewer must focus on.
7. 🧾 PROMPT PRINCIPLE
Prompts are built using: Character + Action (Pattern) + Environment + Style + Lighting.
You MUST use prebuilt prompts blocks from the Annex.
Do NOT invent prompts from scratch when you can reuse.
Ideally, only modify character and environment.
8. 🎨 STYLE SYSTEM
Same style, lighting logic, and color palette across all shots.
Choose one lighting per scene (dark / neutral / intense).
Optional: cinematic framing, depth of field, separation.
9. 🧬 CONSISTENCY SYSTEM
Reuse EXACT same character descriptions (copy-paste).
Keep environments stable and recognizable.
Maintain consistent lighting and visual logic across shots.
Create a “Character Library” file and reuse it systematically.
10. 📚 SERIES-LEVEL SYSTEM
Episodes are part of a continuous story.
Maintain consistency across episodes: characters, clothing, proportions, lighting,
environments.
Reuse assets: prompts, environments, characters, lighting setups.
Maintain an asset library. Reuse instead of recreating.
Result: faster production ×2–3, fewer errors.
11. ⏱ TIMING & WRITING RULES
Shot duration: 3–5 seconds.
Episode: 75–90 seconds.
Line duration = shot duration.
Short ≈3s, medium ≈4s, long ≈5s.

-- 2 of 9 --

Writing rules: expand for rhythm only (no new meaning), everything must be visible, one
idea per shot, add flavor not facts.
12. 🔊 AUDIO & SUBTITLES
Voice must match shot duration exactly, natural pacing, clear articulation.
Subtitles must match voice, be readable in one pass, and remain concise (~10–12 words).
If unreadable → split. If too fast → slow down.
Avoid monotone voice; slight variation improves retention.
13. 🔧 TOOLS & COST-OPTIMIZED STACK
Objective: high volume (10–20 videos/day), near-zero tools cost per video.
Recommended:
• 	ComfyUI (image generation)
• 	DaVinci Resolve (editing)
• 	Kdenlive (lighter editing)
• 	Coqui TTS (voice)
• 	Aegisub (subtitles)
• 	FFmpeg (automation)
Allowed paid tools (only if faster and negligible cost): CapCut, ElevenLabs.
Rule: if cost scales with production → reject.
14. 🔴 FAILURE HANDLING
Level 1: regenerate (max 2 times).
Level 2: simplify prompt.
Level 3: change pattern.
Level 4: escalate.
Max 2–3 minutes per shot.
15. 📊 SCORING GRID
Shot (/20): Anchor (5), Idea (3), Action (3), Readability (5), Consistency (4).
Episode (/50): Shot avg (20), Consistency (10), Flow (10), Speed (10).
Performance:
45–50 ready;
40–44 good;
30–39 supervised;
<30 unusable.
Auto-reject: invisible anchor, static shot, multiple ideas, inconsistency.
Score each shot BEFORE assembling the full episode.

-- 3 of 9 --

16. 🟢 CHECKLIST
Anchor?
Visible instantly?
What moves?
One idea?
Consistent?
If doubt → redo.
17. 📈 PERFORMANCE TARGET
Beginner: 60–90 min/episode.
Week 2: 30–45 min/episode.
Week 3: 20–30 min/episode.
Week 4+: 15–20 min/episode.
The acceleration comes both from your training and from the optimization of libraries and the
reuse of parts.
18. 🧠 FINAL MINDSET
Do not think like an artist. Think like a system operator.
🔥 FINAL RULE
Each shot must answer: “What is the ONE thing the viewer must see?”

-- 4 of 9 --
